doc.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal Interview, 1962-05-24

title: Her father played tuba in a brass band; his funeral
summary: Her father played tuba in an all-brass band that played at his funeral when she was 14; they try to recall the band's name.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Now that would be so long before all of our time. Because my father died when I was 14 years old. And he played in a brass band. My father did. And he played the, what do you call that? The trumpet?
I believe he called it a trumpet or something. What is a trumpet? What is it?
He held it out in front and pushed down.
It was a big horn. It was a horn.

Tuva? Tuva. That big thing. The tuva. That's what he played. It was an all brass band that he launched in. That's no string instrument at all. And I remember they played it at his funeral. His members stayed at his funeral in Dallas. And that was history at that time. Oh, everybody. All the bands played. But you've been around there. Then you've got some history of the can of them. Because they were all out. All out. Yeah.
I've heard of that brass band in my back. Now, now.
What is the name of it? I don't know. You heard of it? Did you hear of it brass band?
I can't think of the name. It's something like the St. James or. St. something.
It was. My father belonged to that band.
I'm telling you. I talked to Freddie Landry for a month there about that band.

Oh, I wonder if it did. I wonder if Mr. James would know. James Landry in the next block. I wonder if he would know. You know, he'd get some doubts, you know. I'm going to ask him and find out, you know. But my father belonged to that band because they played at his funeral. And I was 14 years old when he died. I remember that. Oh, that goes through you. Those bands playing at funerals, you know. That's right. It's so sad. Oh, I wonder why they would do that. And when they hit that drum, oh, it just goes through you. Well, it's a pleasure. And then when they get through, when the person is dead, then they go at home and say, glad you did your rascal you. Glad you did your rascal you.
